question: If the induced EMF in the coil of a conductor of resistance 10 Ω is -2 V, then the induced current in the coil is:

• **Ohm's Law**

 
 
• Ohm's Law states that the current through a conductor between two points is directly proportional to the voltage across the two points.
 
• The law is usually expressed by the equation V=IRV=IR" id="MathJax-Element-78-Frame" role="presentation" style="position: relative;" tabindex="0">V=IR" id="MathJax-Element-185-Frame" role="presentation" style="position: relative;" tabindex="0">V=IR" id="MathJax-Element-53-Frame" role="presentation" style="position: relative;" tabindex="0">V=IR" id="MathJax-Element-56-Frame" role="presentation" style="position: relative;" tabindex="0">V=IR" id="MathJax-Element-20-Frame" role="presentation" style="position: relative;" tabindex="0">V=IR" id="MathJax-Element-68-Frame" role="presentation" style="position: relative;" tabindex="0"> V=IR V=IR V=IR V=IR V=IR V=IR , where V is the voltage, I is the current, and R is the resistance.
 
• This fundamental law is used extensively in electrical engineering and physics to analyze electrical circuits.
 
 
 
• **Electromotive Force (EMF)**
 
 
• Electromotive force (EMF) is the voltage generated by a battery or by the magnetic force according to Faraday's Law.
 
• It is typically denoted by the symbol varepsilonE" id="MathJax-Element-79-Frame" role="presentation" style="position: relative;" tabindex="0">E" id="MathJax-Element-186-Frame" role="presentation" style="position: relative;" tabindex="0">E" id="MathJax-Element-54-Frame" role="presentation" style="position: relative;" tabindex="0">E" id="MathJax-Element-57-Frame" role="presentation" style="position: relative;" tabindex="0">E" id="MathJax-Element-21-Frame" role="presentation" style="position: relative;" tabindex="0">E" id="MathJax-Element-69-Frame" role="presentation" style="position: relative;" tabindex="0">E" id="MathJax-Element-49-Frame" role="presentation" style="position: relative;" tabindex="0"> E E E E E E E \mathcal{E} .
 
• EMF is measured in volts, and it represents the energy provided per coulomb of charge by an energy source.
 
• In the context of electromagnetic induction, EMF is induced when there is a change in magnetic flux.
 
 
 
• **Induced Current**
 
 
• Induced current is the current generated in a conductor due to a changing magnetic field.
 
• According to Faraday's Law of Electromagnetic Induction, the induced EMF in any closed circuit is equal to the negative of the time rate of change of the magnetic flux through the circuit.
 
• Induced current is a fundamental concept in electromagnetism and is utilized in various applications such as transformers, electric generators, and inductors.
